analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/operations/provider-release.md (head lines 632-636). It states that the release lane runs scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py on every built binary before handoff. The script refuses binaries that import Foundation's back-deployed Date.>= or Date.<=, which pre-release macOS 27.2 builds lack. The patch edits no code, workflows or scripts, so it adds no attack surface. It does not alter the signing, notarization, R2 staging, registration, App Attest qualification or revocation flows described elsewhere in the file (TB-009, TB-011, T-054). It does not touch the cache/SSD tier (T-041), the add-on hold socket or the installer boundaries (TB-012, TB-013). The new check is a build-time availability and compatibility guard: it fails the release rather than weakening any control, and it grants no trust. Remaining integration questions: whether the script, the build-guide anchor and the workflow step actually exist and run on every built binary. Those are outside this doc-only patch and were not supplied. If the workflow does not invoke the script as documented, that is documentation drift rather than a security regression. I examined both base text units (lines 1-454 and 455-904) as context for the change. No security-relevant regression was identified.
